reason: Verified in source and by driving the page. render-b.js:214-218 builds .b-undo as three static children — a hardcoded span ("Last change: the invitations moved seven days closer."), a button with no `on` handler, and a kbd reading "Ctrl Z". grep across render-b.js, render-core.js, fixture.js and build.mjs finds no keydown listener anywhere in the lab; the only addEventListener is render-core.js:39's generic `on` binder, which .b-undo never uses. Playwright on ?v=approach&state=owner-editing confirms all four claims: at rest the role=status live region already reads "Last change: the invitations moved seven days closer" (a change that has not happened, announced on arrival); after clicking +7 the item moves 322px -> 420px and .b-away 23 -> 30 while the region text is byte-identical; clicking the Undo button leaves away=30/top=420px; Control+z leaves away=30/top=420px. So the one surface promising reversibility records nothing, reverses nothing, and prints a keystroke that is not bound. This is not restating the gate: interaction-check.mjs:334-338 asserts only existence, uniqueness, role, presence of a button, a kbd matching /ctrl|cmd/, and that the text matches /moved|change/ — every assertion passes on a dead control, which is precisely the blind spot. It breaks no constraint (no colour, weight, family or architecture change) and at a 9.5 bar a fake affordance in the owner's edit loop is a hard defect, not taste.
sharpenedFix: The fix is right in substance; four corrections keep it from breaking things that currently pass. (1) It aims at the wrong seam for the readout: move() already writes the item's top, .b-away and the .b-stepRead text in three places, so undo must not re-implement that. Extract a single setAway(n) inside states['owner-editing'] that is the only writer of data-away, item.style.top, .b-away and read.textContent; have move(delta) call setAway(current+delta) and undo call setAway(entry.fromAway). (2) The proposed announcement wording ("moved from Saturday 8 August to Saturday 1 August") contradicts the state's own grammar — the measure column deliberately carries a bare number and read carries "in N days"; keep the region in that grammar, e.g. "Send the invitations moved to in 30 days. Undo." Also note setAway currently drops the date from read after the first move (rest reads "Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days", post-move reads "in 30 days"); make setAway always write the full date-plus-distance form so undo genuinely restores the exact accessible name rather than a truncated one. (3) Emptying the region at rest WILL break a currently-green gate: interaction-check.mjs:338 ("it says what it would undo") reads el.textContent on a freshly opened owner-editing page and matches /moved|change/. That assertion must be moved to run after one stepper click, with a new at-rest assertion that the region's message span is empty and the Undo button is disabled or absent. Do not leave the region unrendered — .b-undo itself must stay in the DOM so lines 334-337 (exists, exactly one, role=status, names a key) keep passing, and so the live region is present before it has anything to announce. (4) Guard the keydown: only act when (e.ctrlKey||e.metaKey) && e.key.toLowerCase()==='z' && !e.shiftKey AND the active element is not an input/textarea/contenteditable — .b-edit contains #b-edit-title, and hijacking native text undo inside it would trade one defect for another. preventDefault only in the branch that actually pops history. Return focus to the .b-step that made the change, as proposed. New assertions to add: region message empty at rest; names the real change after one move; Ctrl+Z restores exact top, .b-away, .b-stepRead text and focus; Ctrl+Z inside #b-edit-title does not move the item.
